blocks.orig: If you’re reading this, chances are you’ve either travelled solo before or you’re gearing up for one of the most exciting adventures of your life: solo travel in Tanzania. If you’ve never hauled your backpack through an African country on your own, Tanzania is the perfect place to start – and we’ll be at your side from the first idea to the final farewell.
blocks.html: If you have landed on this page, you have probably travelled alone before, or you are preparing for one of the most thrilling adventures of your life: travelling solo in Tanzania. For anyone who has never carried a backpack through an African country alone, Tanzania is the ideal place to begin, and we will be there with you from the very first idea right up to the final goodbye.

blocks.orig: The locals are warm and welcoming, English is widely spoken both in tourist hotspots and sometimes even far beyond, and the infrastructure is solid. And then there’s, of course, the scenery, the wildlife, the mountains, the beaches… we could rave about it forever.
blocks.html: People here are warm and welcoming, English is spoken widely in the tourist hotspots and sometimes well beyond them, and the infrastructure is reliable. On top of that there is the scenery, the wildlife, the mountains, the beaches… honestly, we could go on and on.

blocks.orig: In this guide, we’ll explore the best spots and experiences for solo travellers in Tanzania, share tips to help you prepare, and even give you an idea that might open up a whole new world of possibilities.
blocks.html: This guide looks at the best places and experiences for solo travellers in Tanzania, gives you tips to help you prepare, and ends with an idea that could open up a whole new range of possibilities.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is incredibly diverse, and every region has something worth seeing. So your itinerary really depends on what you want to experience.
blocks.html: Tanzania is enormously varied and each region has something worth seeing, so your route really depends on what you would like to experience.

blocks.orig: Lake Manyara is popular for its tree-climbing lions and colourful birdlife, while Ruaha and Nyerere offer less crowded safaris filled with the Big Five, wild dogs, crocodiles, hippos and more. While Nyerere is shaped by the Rufiji River, Ruaha wows with its vast, rugged landscapes.
blocks.html: Lake Manyara is known for its tree-climbing lions and colourful birdlife, whereas Ruaha and Nyerere offer less crowded safaris packed with the Big Five, wild dogs, crocodiles, hippos and more. Nyerere is defined by the Rufiji River, while Ruaha impresses with its vast, rugged landscapes.

blocks.orig: And if you’re feeling adventurous, you can always embark on a trek to the summit of the famous Mount Kilimanjaro.
blocks.html: Feeling adventurous? You could always set off on a trek to the top of the famous Mount Kilimanjaro.

blocks.orig: For classic safaris and abundant wildlife with minimal travel time between parks, the Northern Circuit is great, with Arusha or Tarangire National Park as ideal starting points.
blocks.html: If you are after classic safaris and plenty of wildlife with little travel time between parks, the Northern Circuit is an excellent choice, with Arusha or Tarangire National Park as the ideal starting point.

blocks.orig: While the months December to February and June to October are considered the best months to visit Tanzania (dry season), the other months have their perks, too. It really just comes down to what you want to see and how flexible your budget is. You can find a full overview here.
blocks.html: The months from December to February and June to October are generally seen as the best time to visit Tanzania (the dry season), but the other months have their advantages too. In the end it comes down to what you want to see and how flexible your budget is. A full overview is available here.

blocks.orig: You can use US dollars at touristy places, but it’s still smart to carry some Tanzanian shillings, especially outside cities, where ATMs can be scarce. Most accommodations offer Wi-Fi, but getting a local SIM card will keep you connected throughout your trip (even if your plan is to unplug). Data speeds are good in cities and along the coast, and a bit patchier in national parks. You can buy SIM cards at the airport or in town from Vodacom, Airtel, or Tigo; just bring your passport.
blocks.html: US dollars are accepted in touristy spots, yet it is wise to keep some Tanzanian shillings on you, particularly outside the cities where ATMs can be few and far between. Most places to stay have Wi-Fi, but a local SIM card keeps you connected for the whole trip (even if your intention is to switch off). Data is fast in the cities and along the coast, and somewhat patchy in the national parks. SIM cards from Vodacom, Airtel or Tigo are sold at the airport and in town; remember to bring your passport.

blocks.orig: Is Tanzania safe for solo female travellers?
blocks.html: Is Tanzania safe for women travelling alone?

blocks.orig: Tanzania is generally safe for solo female travellers, especially in popular areas like Arusha, Zanzibar, and the northern safari parks. As with any destination, a few smart precautions can make your trip even safer. And by the way: these tips apply to all solo travellers. 😉
blocks.html: On the whole, Tanzania is safe for solo female travellers, particularly in well-visited areas such as Arusha, Zanzibar and the northern safari parks. As anywhere, a few sensible precautions make your trip safer still. And for the record, these tips are meant for every solo traveller. 😉

blocks.orig: Follow these simple guidelines, and you’ll be able to enjoy Tanzania with confidence. With so much to see and do in this East African gem, exploring it solo can truly be unforgettable.
blocks.html: Stick to these simple guidelines and you can enjoy Tanzania with confidence. With so much to see and do in this East African gem, a solo trip here can be truly unforgettable.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar is only for families and honeymooners? Think again! Zanzibar offers plenty of activities for solo travellers. From snorkelling and water sports to lounging on the beach, burying your feet in the sand, and sipping a cocktail with a little umbrella… there’s something for everyone.
blocks.html: Is Zanzibar just for families and honeymooners? Not at all! The island has lots to offer solo travellers. Snorkelling, water sports, lazing on the beach with your toes in the sand, a cocktail with a tiny umbrella in it… there is something here for everyone.

blocks.orig: Activities for solo travellers in Zanzibar
blocks.html: Things to do in Zanzibar on your own

blocks.orig: Jambiani and Paje on the east coast of Zanzibar are perfect for beach life galore. Many little restaurants, bars and live music set the scene for kicking back and maybe even making new friends (even if it’s just for the day). You can also visit the Kua Cave, take a cooking class or go for a bike ride. And obviously, you can always jump into the sea and meet colourful fish.
blocks.html: On Zanzibar’s east coast, Jambiani and Paje are ideal for beach life in abundance. Plenty of small restaurants, bars and live music create the right mood for unwinding and perhaps making new friends (even if only for a day). You could also visit the Kua Cave, join a cooking class or head out on a bike. And of course the sea is always there, full of colourful fish waiting to be met.

blocks.orig: If you want to explore Stone Town, simply join a tour through this diverse city and learn more about its history, its culture and fun facts. Combine it with a spice farm tour and this day will be one for the books.
blocks.html: Keen to discover Stone Town? Simply join a guided tour of this diverse city and hear about its history, its culture and some fun facts along the way. Pair it with a spice farm tour and you have a day to remember.
